principles: Every completed item must be mechanically traceable to the document commitment it closes.
Finish the full ProofStory commitments inside the existing Lattice lifecycle rather than adding a second lifecycle.
Prefer compact gate-consumed artifacts over an autopilot scheduler or automatic child-story creation.
Keep risk-adaptive rollout semantics: simple stories stay light, enforce mode becomes mechanically meaningful.
drivers: User explicitly requested complete M0-M9 closure with per-item document cross-check before each completion mark.
The previous B-f7b7 story was DONE as MVP but left full-document commitments incomplete.
Future open-source users need English prompts/docs and mechanically auditable behavior.

options.name: A: Implement compact artifacts and gate semantics now
pros: Closes the concrete document gaps without overbuilding orchestration
Keeps the existing Lattice lifecycle and review gates authoritative
Allows smoke and process-fact tests to prove the behavior
cons: Requires touching several core files, handlers, prompts, and smoke tests in one story

options.name: B: Only update docs to clarify future scope
pros: Smaller change and lower immediate risk
cons: Would not satisfy the user request to develop until fully complete

options.name: C: Build a full scheduler and automatic child-story system now
pros: Could eventually support large epics end to end
cons: Too large for this follow-up and risks creating a second lifecycle/state machine

chosen: A: Implement compact artifacts and gate semantics now
rationale: Choose compact implementation because it closes the audited M0-M9 gaps while preserving the existing lifecycle. Slice-plan and parent-rollup artifacts are enough for gate-consumed proof; automatic scheduling can remain a separate future capability.

preMortem.scenario: Scope expands into a full scheduler
preMortem.trigger: Implementing slice-plan starts auto-creating child stories or parallel workers
preMortem.consequence: The story becomes too broad and risks a second lifecycle
preMortem.mitigation: Implement only slice-plan and roll-up artifacts plus diagnostics; no automatic child story creation.

preMortem.scenario: Checklist item is marked done without document proof
preMortem.trigger: A developer relies on memory or smoke coverage only
preMortem.consequence: User requirement is violated and the audit becomes untrustworthy
preMortem.mitigation: Before every checklist_update done, record document line evidence, implementation evidence, and verification evidence in the completion note.

preMortem.scenario: Prompt-only rules drift from gate behavior
preMortem.trigger: Reviewer prompts mention ProofStory but no process-fact or smoke test covers it
preMortem.consequence: Future agents trust text that gates do not enforce
preMortem.mitigation: Update process-fact contract and smoke coverage for every gate-consumed behavior.

preMortem.trigger: DONE equivalence or red/spike checks require heavy artifacts for simple single-outcome work
preMortem.consequence: ProofStory becomes too expensive for normal development
preMortem.mitigation: Implement lightweight single-outcome DONE equivalence and keep red/spike/collision trigger-based.
